BiblicalUsage: Chalaqqah is flattery, and it appears once: those who do wickedly against the covenant will be corrupted by flatteries, but the people who know their God will be strong and do exploits.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe flattery corrupts the covenant-breaker and cannot touch the one who knows his God — that is the whole verse in one line.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
